pillar_reactions.evidence: The prospect tied the modality directly to his own goal without being asked: 'I want to be a bit big, but I want to be ripped as well though, like six pack and muscles and stuff' in response to the fighter-physique framing. He was visibly sold by the founder proof — 'if he really like what he says, like, he don't go to the gym. And that's his body then. That's crazy to me' — and by the rep's own three-month before-and-after photos: 'Oh, that's crazy.' Mobility was folded in as injury prevention and posture and drew no reaction of its own.

Delivered briefly — 'we eat for health... when you're healthy inside, like losing fat and getting in shape is just a side effect... We're not eating chicken, rice, and broccoli seven times a day' — and received with 'Yeah. Yeah. Okay.' No questions, despite the prospect having said food was fifty per cent of the problem and that he did not know what to eat. The pillar he most needed got the least airtime.

24/7 access to Trevor and weekly adjustment were presented in full, closing on 'It's like having a teacher there next to you the whole time' — answered 'Yeah.' Worth noting the prospect's live reaction mid-pitch was overload rather than reassurance: 'I'm confused now just speaking about it. Never mind', to which the rep answered 'I'll keep it super simple for you.'

anchors.raw: No, it's like a, I think it's like a 12-week program, yeah? To guarantee get you ripped. It's called FLF Performance Center. It's, it's, man, it's crazy. Like, every training, it's like, wow, like, how is that even possible in 12 weeks?
anchors.note: A named, guaranteed, twelve-week transformation programme was in the prospect's head before the call, and he confirmed the timeframe was what he wanted: 'That's what I was really looking for.' It sets an expectation of a quarter of the duration for an unstated but implicitly gym-membership-scale price, which is the frame $6,000 for six months had to land against. He also mentioned researching HIIT programmes for the same reason.

anchors.raw: I don't have, like, a personal coach tell me, like, you have to eat this on this day, this week, do that, you know, like, that kind of thing.
anchors.note: The prospect has never paid for coaching, never held a gym membership beyond about a week, and runs a cash-based convenience store where he keeps little in the bank. There is no reference point in his experience for a four-figure coaching purchase, and the rep never built one before naming the price.

unmet_demand.want: His wife, approximately one year postpartum, to follow the same programme and diet alongside him for her own weight loss — asked twice: 'Can my wife do this with me?' and 'she said my like my wife can do the exact same workout as me like'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep answered yes to both the nutrition and the training without qualifying it — 'She can do all the food with you, she can do the training with you if she wants to do the training' — but the offer as described is one-to-one coaching with Trevor for a single named client. Scope, whether she gets any tailoring or assessment, and whether a second person is permitted at all were never addressed, and no price was discussed.

unmet_demand.want: A twelve-week outcome rather than a six-month commitment
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The minimum term offered is six months at $6,000. The rep argued the shorter route sacrifices muscle gain, which reframes the timeframe but does not serve the want: there is no twelve-week product.
